71958.title: Greenwood Branch AGM
71958.description: The Greenwood Branch AGM will be held on Wednesday, 27 May, 2026 at Paddy’s Pub in Kentville, Nova Scotia, in the private events room upstairs. Members are invited for 5:00pm with the meeting being called to order at 5:30pm. We expect the meeting to be over by 7:00pm. Refreshments and your choice of dinner items off the menu will be provided free of cost. RSVPs to chad.lacoste@forces.gc.ca are requested so we can let the venue know approximately how many will be in attendance. If you do not RSVP, you are still more than welcome to attend the AGM so please come if you have the time! Notice of Elections: Elections will be held at the Greenwood Branch AGM to fill five vacancies on the executive. All positions are for a two-year term. The positions up for election this year are: Vice President, Treasurer, and three Member-at-large positions. Chad Lacoste will be over-seeing the elections. Nominations for positions may be done in advance by emailing Chad at chad.lacoste@forces.gc.ca Volunteers and nominations will be accepted from the floor at the AGM as well. Thank-you and hopefully we will see you there. Chad Lacoste Greenwood Branch – President Atlantic Regional Executive – Member at Large Southwest Nova IT Sub-group – Vice President Steward

73153.title: Fredericton SP Subgroup 2026 Annual General Meeting – May 11, 2026
73153.description: All SP members in the Fredericton/Oromocto area are cordially invited by the Fredericton SP Sub-Group Executive to join us for our Annual General Meeting. DATE: Monday, May 11th, 2026 WHERE: The Fedora Room-The Kingswood Lodge, 31 Kingswood Park, Fredericton, NB WHEN: 6:30 PM-8:30 PM Agenda: 1 Introductions 2 Approval of Agenda 3 Approval of Previous AGM Minutes 4 President and Treasurer’s Reports (Budget Approval) 5 Guest Speaker (SP Executive Team Member) 6 Election of Officers – President (2 Year Term), Secretary (2 Year Term) and Member-at-Large(s) (4, 1 Year Term) – Nominations to be made from floor of AGM, please reach out to an executive member if you would like to run but can’t make meeting 7 New Business/Q&A Dinner and refreshments will be provided by the Fredericton SP Subgroup Executive. Kingswood will provide menus which participants can order from. RSVP If you are interested in attending or have any questions you may RSVP via e-mail or in person to anyone on the executive by Friday, May 8, 2026: Marcus Peck- marcus.peck@dal.ca Emily Nicholson- beautysparadiseleather@gmail.com Mark Bennett- mbennett@pipcsc.ca Marcus Mclaughlin- mmclaughlin@pipsc.ca Deanna McCullum – deanna.mccullum@forces.gc.ca Ty Hardy – thardy@ualberta.ca Bradley Crealman – crealmanbjc@gmail.com

73431.title: Halifax IT Sub-Group Annual General Meeting – June 4, 2026
73431.description: The Halifax IT Sub-Group Annual General Meeting will be held on June 4th, 2026, at the Lion’s Head Tavern (3085 Robie St, Halifax, NS B3K 4P7). Doors open at 5:30 PM for networking, with the meeting starting at 6:00 PM. Additional details are available on our web page. Attendance requires an RSVP by May 21. To register, email HalifaxITSubGroup@pipsc.ca. For questions, contact the union executive at HalifaxITSubGroup@pipsc.ca. This yearly meeting gives members an opportunity to discuss current challenges facing Public Service employees, including contract negotiations and workforce adjustment. In solidarity, Executive Halifax IT Sub-Group, PIPSC

73946.title: Webinar: WFA and mental health support
73946.description: As Work Force Adjustments (WFAs) continue to affect members across the public service, mental health is top of mind. Active members like you provide a safe space to share emotions and lived experiences. That emotional labour can be difficult to manage, which is why we want to provide tools and resources to help you navigate mental health in the workplace. PIPSC has teamed up with the Canadian Mental Health Association to offer you a custom online training on mental health foundations to help you support your peers and take care of yourself. When: Thursday, May 14, from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM ET (bilingual session) RSVP In this session, you will learn to: Use respectful language and raise awareness of mental health Recognize signs and symptoms of mental health challenges Apply prevention and protective strategies Have safe, supportive conversations and seek help This will be a bilingual training session with simultaneous interpretation and a bilingual facilitator. If you can’t make it, visit our mental health resource page and keep an eye out for the recording, which will be posted on our website. If you have questions about the training, please contact bettertogether@pipsc.ca.

74093.title: RTO Solidarity Lunch: May the curds be with you!
74093.description: On May 4, we’re showing up – together – to push back against the federal government’s return-to-office (RTO) mandate. This isn’t about just one more day in the office. This is about working conditions and respect for the people who provide the public services Canadians rely on. This is about the lack of meaningful consultations. We’re standing with all colleagues in Ottawa to show that this mandate isn’t working for anyone. Join us for a “presence with purpose” lunch in solidarity with fellow members. We’ll be at Lou’s Food Truck handing out free poutine and fries until we run out. Bring your coworkers, stop by during your lunch break, and be part of a visible show of support. When: Monday, May 4, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM Where: Lou’s Food Truck, Kent Street near Slater Street, Ottawa, ON. RSVP No matter where you stand on RTO, this impacts more than just where we do our work. We want the biggest employer in Canada to be a model employer. One where: telework agreements help diversify the workforce, so our public service truly reflects the geography and demographics of Canada evidence-based decision-making is the standard, so the employer stops putting politics over strengthening public services employer and employee relationships are respectful, consultative and transparent, so we can continue to deliver our best while trusting that our employer has our back If you can’t make it on May 4, you can still take action against RTO by sending your MP a message: https://pipsc.

75223.description: You’re invited to Steps for Science: A rally against WFA and RTO4 in Vancouver! It takes experts to run a country. When scientists are cut, risks increase. Cuts today, crisis tomorrow. Rally with your PIPSC SP colleagues outside 401 Burrard Street in Vancouver to protect our critical systems and stand up for our scientific experts. 75882.description: Dear Montérégie members, The Montérégie Branch is pleased to offer its members an information session on the basic concepts of the pension plan for employees of the federal government. This is not the advanced retirement planning course. This session is intended especially for new employees of the federal public service as well as for members who wish to gain a better understanding of the fundamentals of their pension plan. The session will be led by the Montérégie Branch Vice-President, Steve Parent. Since this session is free and optional, members who wish to participate do not need to register. Simply connect to the Zoom link below about five minutes before the session begins. We look forward to seeing many of you there. https://pipsc.zoom.us/j/91541767750?pwd=um0QwIqLzWLyTFEqrwzaHX0j8lGwal.1 Meeting ID: 915 4176 7750 Passcode: 184510 Date: Tuesday, June 9, 2026 (presentation in French only) Where: Virtual Time: 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.

76304.title: Vancouver Branch Hike and National Indigenous Peoples Day meetup
76304.description: You’re invited to a Vancouver Branch hike and National Indigenous Peoples Day meetup! The Vancouver Branch is planning a summer hike series, beginning with a morning hike to Norvan Falls followed by the National Indigenous Peoples Day event in Ambleside Park in the evening. You are welcome to either or both meetups! Norvan Falls Hike When: Sunday, June 21, at 10:00 AM PT Where: Meetup location will be provided to confirmed participants Details: The hike is approximately 14 km with 358 m of elevation gain, will take 4-6 hours, and is considered moderate difficulty. Please see AllTrails for more information. National Indigenous Peoples Day When: Sunday, June 21, at 4:00 PM PT Where: Squamish Nation Welcome Figure, Ambleside Park, West Vancouver Details: The event includes family activities and live music. To RSVP and for more information, please contact Elmira Nazar at enazar@pipsc.ca.

76357.title: French webinar: Work Force Adjustment and Return to Office
76357.description: You are invited to a special French-language virtual event on Work Force Adjustment and Return to Office taking place on Thursday, June 11, 2026, from 6:30 PM to 8:00 PM on Zoom. Speakers Sean O’Reilly, PIPSC President Katie Francis, PIPSC Vice-President Dejan Toncic, Acting Manager, National Policy Office The speakers will provide members with up-to-date information on developments related to: Work Force Adjustment and Return to Office the work PIPSC is doing to support affected members, and PIPSC campaigns to fight back and defend our members Jointly organized with PIPSC executive members and volunteers from the National Capital Region, this event is intended for French-speaking members across the country. We invite you to share this invitation with your Francophone colleagues. No advance registration is required. However, we encourage you to log in a few minutes early to avoid any technical issues. Join now (Zoom link) Meeting ID: 999 5181 7165 Passcode: 588856 For any questions or technical issues when logging in, please contact Stéphane Audet at saudet@pipsc.ca.

76401.title: Atlantic Young Professionals Committee Virtual Information Session: Atlantic Regional Director
76401.description: Please join the Atlantic Young Professionals Committee (for members 40 and under) for a virtual information session with Guest Speaker, Atlantic Regional Director, Mark Bellefleur on Wednesday, June 24, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. Atlantic Time. An RSVP is required for this event. Please RSVP to Natasha Cabot at ncabot@pipsc.ca by June 22, 2026. A link to the session will be emailed to you if you RSVP prior to the information session. If you would like to submit a question beforehand, please do so in your RSVP. There will be a door prize drawn from the participants in attendance.

76456.title: Coffee break for PIPSC members at Bedford Institute of Oceanography
76456.description: All PIPSC members at the Bedford Institute of Oceanography are invited to a coffee break during National Public Service Week. Join us for a hot or cold beverage and some treats. Local stewards and representatives of the Halifax CP Sub-Group and the Mainland Nova Scotia SP Sub-Group will be available to answer any questions. No registration is required. Tuesday June 16th 2026, 10-11 am in the Katherine Ellis Lobby. This event is sponsored by the PIPSC Halifax Branch. If you have questions please contact Olga Trela at otrela@pipsc.ca.

76822.title: Halifax Tides Soccer Game
76822.description: You are invited to the Halifax Tides Soccer game on Saturday, June 13, 2026 at 1:30pm at the Wanderers Grounds. Tickets: Adult Ticket: $36.37 tax inclusive (regular price $52.99) Youth Ticket: $29.42 tax inclusive (regular price $38.77) Tickets can be purchased at: Halifax Tides Soccer PIPSC. Member Benefit: Active members will be responsible to purchase their ticket(s) to attend the event and as a benefit receive a Tim Hortons gift card(s) for $15 when purchasing a ticket, to a maximum of 2 gift cards. Furthermore, to receive the gift card(s), the name on the ticket purchase must be the active PIPSC member and may be subject to verification prior to receiving the gift cards. Although a maximum of 2 gift cards will be given out, members can buy as many tickets as they want. There are a limited number of gift cards available and they will be given out on a first come first serve basis. If we reach the maximum number of gift cards before June 11, 2026, tickets may still be purchased, but no gift cards will be received. Gift cards will be able to be picked up on game day at the event. An email will be distributed the week before game day with the details. Note: Tickets will be sent electronically from the Tides. If you do not receive the tickets, you will be responsible for contacting the Tides directly. If you have any questions or concerns for the event, please contact the organizer: Alex Payne, Member (member at large) at apayne@pipsc.ca

76830.title: Webinar: Return-to-Office: Know Your Rights
76830.description: As the Return-to-Office (RTO) mandate continues to affect us all, staying informed and engaged is crucial. We’re hosting a webinar to update you on how we’re supporting members and ensure you know your workplace rights. RTO Know Your Rights Webinar June 10 at 12:00 PM ET RSVP NOW In this webinar, we will discuss: updates on PIPSC’s efforts against the RTO mandate critical insights into how RTO influences our bargaining position actionable advice on how you can defend your rights and participate in the process Learn more about Return to Workplaces: Know Your Rights About Returning To The Office FAQ: Returning To The Workplace If you have any questions, please email bettertogether@pipsc.ca.

78576.title: PIPSC Pride Webinar 2026
78576.description: In celebration of Pride Month, PIPSC is hosting a webinar on June 25, 2026, to educate members about the federal government’s “LGBT Purge” and the ongoing challenges and resilience of 2SLGBTQIA+ communities. Between the 1950s and mid-1990s, 2SLGBTQIA+ members of the Canadian Armed Forces, the RCMP, and the federal public service were systematically discriminated against, harassed, and often fired in what came to be known as the “LGBT Purge”. Workers were followed, interrogated, abused, and traumatized. This Pride Month, we invite members to a webinar about the experiences of 2SLGBTQIA+ workers in the federal government. Simultaneous interpretation will be provided in English and French. When: June 25, 2026, at 1:00 PM ETWhere: Zoom RSVP NOW Meeting ID: 948 0548 4959Passcode: 31159 Panelists include LGBT Purge survivor France Bergeron from the Canadian Armed Forces and retired Navy Commander Treena Scurlock. Together, let’s honour Pride Month – not just as a celebration, but as a call to action for ongoing progress.

79815.description: The Halifax Branch and the Halifax DND Branch Executives, invite you to join us for a special meet and greet with David Sutherland, part-time Vice President. Date: July 24, 2026 Time: 4:30-6:30pm Location: The Pint (https://thepinthfx.com/) Dave has been a dedicated member of PIPSC and actively supports our Young Professional Committees. He is passionate about Return to Office and advocates work-life balance. Dave also brings significant expertise in Workforce Adjustment (WFA), providing valuable guidance and support during these challenging times. Dave values collaboration and respect, always relying on facts and expert advice for tough decisions. Dave aims to strengthen relationships within PIPSC and welcomes the opportunity to connect with you in person. Please register here by July 21st We look forward to seeing you there.

80424.title: Call for Nominations — Steward Recognition Award 2026
80424.description: Stewards are the backbone of our union. As volunteers, they serve as vital links between our members, the employer, and the union—offering support, guidance, and advocacy that helps improve our workplaces. To recognize their efforts, we invite members in the Prairie/NWT Region to nominate a steward who has demonstrated exceptional dedication, time, and commitment to our union and fellow members. How It Works: All nominations received will be reviewed by a regional committee. Input from Employment Relations Officers (EROs), who regularly work with stewards, may also be considered. From these nominations, stewards whose efforts meet the selection criteria will be recognized with a commemorative memento at our upcoming Regional Steward Council. One exceptional nominee will be chosen as the Steward of the Year, to be honored at the PIPSC Annual General Meeting in Toronto. Eligibility:Nominees must be stewards located in the Prairie/NWT Region and must have actively served as a steward for at least one year. Who Can Nominate:Regular members and EROs are eligible to submit nominations. Each nomination must include: Nominator’s full name, phone number, and email address Steward’s full name and contact information A written submission (max. 300 words) describing the steward’s contributions and qualities Selection Criteria: Nominees will be evaluated based on their involvement in activities such as: welcoming new employees and encouraging PIPSC membership; engaging RANDs to sign membe

80802.title: Halifax Pride Parade
80802.description: PIPSC members are invited to march with us in the Halifax Pride Parade in support of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community. This year, PIPSC will be joining the Nova Scotia Federation of Labour (NSFL) and will be marching alongside fellow union members from organizations such as CAPE, PSAC, and others. Family members and friends are welcome to participate as well. We hope you’ll join us for this celebration of diversity, inclusion, and solidarity! We are also pleased to be joined by Katie Francis, one of PIPSC’s Full-Time Vice-Presidents and a member of the Institute’s Board of Directors. Katie Francis is currently in her three-year term, helping to guide the strategic direction of PIPSC and advance key initiatives on behalf of members. Her portfolios include Return-to-Office (RTO), Phoenix, and Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI). Looking forward to seeing you there!Parade Date: Saturday, July 18, 2026 Location: Parade Mustering Grounds – 5775 Cogswell St., Halifax, NS. Our parade spot is C24, and you will find us in the parade mustering grounds, which are located along Cogswell Street, between Robie Street and North Park Street. Time: We will start gathering at 11:00 am. The parade starts at noon, but it’s important that volunteers are in place ahead of that time. Additional Info: Make sure to dress for the weather, pack a reusable water bottle, plenty of sunscreen and a hat. To register, please fill out this form by end of day, July 17, 2026. If you have questions, please contact Olg

80842.title: Return to office – Complimentary mice and BYO-Desk
80842.description: Join us at the corner of Bank Street and Laurier Avenue in Ottawa, as we spread the word about workplace health and safety concerns you’ve shared with us. When: July 8 from 12:00 to 1:00 PM ET Where: Corner of Laurier Avenue and Bank Street, Ottawa RSVP NOW We’ll have treats and information about your rights regarding RTO. You’ll also learn how to participate in our RTO sticker contest – stick it, post a photo, tag PIPSC, and you could win a prize! We’ve heard hundreds of stories about: offices that feel like construction sites employees being forced to work from cafeterias and crowded cubicles outdated government offices with pest problems, and more Let’s continue to push back against this one-size-fits-all approach, which lacks evidence to support it, puts workers’ health and safety at risk, and undermines employee productivity. If you have any questions, please email Kfrancis@pipsc.ca.

81115.description: We are pleased to offer an Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) training in addition to the employer training you may have received. As we are limited to twenty participants, we will use selection criteria to select the participants. We encourage you to submit your application form as soon as you receive the email. LOCATION: Calgary, Alta TIME: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (All participants are required to attend the full session) APPLICATION DEADLINE: August 14, 2026 APPLICATION FORM: https://forms.gle/mzictDaLCpAE46nv6 After the application deadline, the training committee will review your application, if selected to attend we will send you a registration invite. 81690.title: PIPSC Halifax Branch – 20th Annual Golf Classic and Fall Social
81690.description: The PIPSC Halifax Branch is pleased to invite its members, as well as members of the Halifax DND Branch, and their guests to the 20th Annual Golf Classic and Fall Social, taking place at the beautiful Granite Springs Golf Club in Bayside, Nova Scotia. Participants are invited to enjoy a round of 18 holes of golf, followed by an informal BBQ dinner. Tee-offs will be arranged in groups of four players. Participants may register as a group of four or register individually and be placed into a group where space permits. Golf tournament awards and door prizes will be presented near the end of the meal. Participation in the golf tournament is not required to attend the BBQ dinner. However, only those who are registered for the BBQ dinner and are in attendance will be eligible for door prizes. As part of our 20th Annual Golf Classic and Fall Social, we will be holding a voluntary fundraiser in support of the PIPSC Legacy Foundation. The Foundation provides scholarships to the children and grandchildren of PIPSC members pursuing post-secondary education. We encourage everyone to participate and help invest in the future of our PIPSC community.Event DetailsLocation:Granite Springs Golf Club, 4441 Prospect Road, Bayside, NSDate: Monday, September 14, 2026Registration Deadline:Monday, September 7, 2026Golf Tournament: 1:00 p.m. – Modified shotgun startBBQ Dinner:5:30 p.m. approximately, immediately following the golf tournament CostsAll prices include HST.Golf fees and shared cart renta

82322.title: Health Canada (NCR) Branch Networking Event:
82322.description: Summer Picnic 2026 Date: Saturday, August 29, 2026 Time: 11:30 am – 2.00 pm Where: Britannia Park and Beach – Long Gazebo, 2805 Carling Ave, Ottawa, ON K2B 8K6 Dear Member, The Health Canada (NCR) Branch is pleased to invite you and your immediate family to our 2026 Summer Picnic! Join fellow Health Canada members and their families from worksites across the National Capital Region for a relaxing day of networking, conversation, and fun at one of the NCR’s most beautiful parks. It’s a wonderful opportunity to connect with colleagues, share ideas, discuss our common goals, and hear the latest updates on the Return-to-Office plan. Enjoy a complimentary picnic lunch, soft drinks, and dessert, served between 12:00 p.m. and 1:30 p.m., while spending quality time with family and friends in a welcoming outdoor setting. We look forward to seeing you there for a great day of community, connection, and summer fun! As space is limited, please complete the required information below and submit it to Helmi Hussien hhussien@pipsc.ca by Friday, August 22, 2026. Name: Number Of Immediate Family: Group (e.g. SP / IT / RE): Membership Number: Worksite: Email Address: We respectfully ask that if you have RSVP’d attendance, but circumstances change, kindly advise us at the same email address to cancel. 82346.title: Mauricie Branch- Pumpkin Hunt Activity- Sunday, September 27, 2026
82346.description: INVITATION TO A PUMPKIN Hunt Activity Dear PIPSC members, What better way to enjoy the autumn season than by spending time outdoors with your family? Your union’s Mauricie Branch is pleased to invite you to a pumpkin hunt outing at Ferme Éthier in Saint-Étienne-des-Grès! Location: Ferme Éthier – Les Fruits Soleil Address: 490 4e Rang, Saint-Étienne-des-Grès, QC G0X 2P0 Date: Sunday, September 27, 2026 Arrival time: Between 9:30 a.m. and 10:30 a.m. It’s the perfect time to pick out and decorate your pumpkins for Halloween. This activity is free for PIPSC members and their families. What’s included? Site access and one pumpkin per participant (e.g., a family of 3 gets 3 pumpkins). Come enjoy the autumn atmosphere, pick out your best pumpkins, and share a pleasant time with your colleagues and their loved ones. On-site: local produce stalls, children’s activities, and much more! Please confirm your interest by September 15, 2026 using this address: sectionmauricie@pipsc.ca We look forward to seeing many of you there! Your Mauricie Branch Executive

82399.title: Beauty & The Beast
82399.description: ***We have reached the maximum number of complimentary tickets. Members may register to be placed on a waiting list or may purchase tickets through e-transfer to hashem.aboushahla@gmail.com*** The Halifax Branch is delighted to invite you and a guest to a live, outdoor performance of “Beauty and the Beast” presented by Shakespeare By The Sea. The show will take place at Point Pleasant Park on Thursday, August 20th at 7:00 pm. Complimentary snacks and water will be provided courtesy of the Halifax Branch. To RSVP, please fill out the registration form by Friday, August 14th with your name, email address, membership number, department, and number of attendees. Seats are limited to 2 per member and are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Please note that because tickets are limited, members who register but do not attend will be required to repay the ticket cost. If you need extra seats, they can be purchased at a preferred rate of $25 each (regularly $34.20) by sending an e-transfer to hashem.aboushahla@gmail.com by August 14th (please include “SBTS” and your name in the memo line). Since this is an outdoor event, our rain date is set for Sunday, August 23rd at 7:00 pm. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to Hashem at hashem.aboushahla@gmail.com. We hope to see you there

82675.title: PIPSC Labour Day Parade
82675.description: The PIPSC National Capital Region (NCR) will be marching together in this year’s Labour Day Parade, and we would love to see a strong, proud, and enthusiastic turnout from our members. Event Details Monday, September 7, 2026 Assembly Time: Please arrive no later than 11:30 a.m. March Start: 12:00 p.m. sharp March Starting point: Ottawa City Hall (Lisgar Street Side) March End Point: McNabb Park March Distance: Approximately 2.2 km If you are unable to participate in the march but would still like to show your support and solidarity, we invite you to join us at McNabb Park at 1:00 p.m. This is a wonderful opportunity to stand together in support of fair workplaces, respect, equity, and the rights of all workers. 82685.title: Pride during Capital Pride: The NCR will screen Matthew Warchus’ Pride (2014)
82685.description: National Capital Region (NCR) Pride during Capital Pride: The NCR will screen Matthew Warchus’ Pride (2014) Join us for a screening of the film Pride (2014), a film about the 2SLGBTQIA+ alliance that supported the National Union of Mineworkers, during the year-long UK miners’ strike of 1984–1985. Pride, directed by Matthew Warchus, is based on the true story of an alliance of lesbian and gay activists who travel to the small Welsh mining village of Onllwyn, in a show of intercommunity solidarity. Pride was named the Best British Independent Film of 2014 and The New York Times called the film a “hearty, blunt-force drama with softened edges that leaves audiences applauding and teary-eyed.” Come celebrate Capital Pride with your union family at Ottawa’s historic Mayfair Theatre, one of the oldest surviving independent movie houses in all of Canada. Whether you’re a long-time activist or newly involved in the union, this is a great opportunity to connect with fellow members, deepen your understanding of labour history, and celebrate the collective power of working people. DATE: August 27, 2026 TIME: 6:30 – 9:00 PM (Door opens at 6:00 PM) MEETING LOCATION: The Mayfair Theatre (1074 Bank Street, Ottawa) Register here! “Best regards, Email: cpalmer@pipsc.ca

83523.title: GTA Chapter of the Retired Members Guild Summer Social Event
83523.description: Greetings to our retired PIPSC brothers and sisters! It’s been a while since we last met at our AGM back in October 2025. As such, we are pleased to invite you to join us at our Chapter’s social event at the Sababa Restaurant (Middle Eastern fare). Date: Wednesday, August 26, 2026 Time: 12:30 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. Location: Sababa Restaurant Address: 390 Steeles Ave. W. (north side of Steeles, just west of Hilda Ave.). Lots of free parking. Lunch Lunch is on us! Taxes and gratuities are on us (total value approximately $21).Generally, lunch will consist of a pita bread sandwich, fries, and a soft drink, coffee, or tea. Attendees will be billed separately for alcoholic beverages. A menu is available online; a few additional pita sandwich choices will also be available. About the Event This is purely a social event. There will be no guest speakers and no formal agenda.However, there is still lots to talk about. 84880.title: Halifax Branch Labour Day Rally
84880.description: Please join us in celebrating Labour Day. The Halifax-Dartmouth and District Labour Council is hosting this year’s local events on Monday, September 7, and PIPSC Halifax Branch will be marching and celebrating together. ​Event Schedule: ​Rally @ 11AM: Gathering outside the Nova Scotia Labour Board (Summit Place, 1601 Lower Water St.) ​March: Following the rally, we’ll march together down to Peace & Friendship Park (Hollis St.) ​Picnic: A community picnic at Peace & Friendship Park featuring free food, drinks, live entertainment, and family activities like face painting and a bouncy castle. Bring your family and friends, wear your PIPSC colours, and come out for a fun afternoon in the sun. We’ll also have PIPSC swag on hand to give out. ​Hope to see you there. ​Best regards,​Hashem Abou-ShahlaHalifax Branch President

84912.title: Join the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation’s (NCTR) Remembering the Children commemoration
84912.description: Join our commemoration of the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (Orange Shirt Day) on September 30. Hear from survivors and Elders, and learn more about the impacts of the residential school system. When: September 30, 2026 from 11:00 AM to end of day. Where: We will meet at the National Aboriginal Veterans Monument in Confederation Park, across from the Lord Elgin Hotel (100 Elgin Street, Ottawa), and walk to Parliament Hill. Please RSVP here by September 19, 2026. This helps us plan for the event. Our commemoration begins with an Indigenous prayer and smudging ceremony at Confederation Park, followed by a walk to Parliament Hill for the live APTN broadcast with speakers from the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation (NCTR). We have a limited number of orange sweatshirts and T-shirts. If you already have an orange PIPSC sweatshirt, please wear it to the event, weather permitting. Light snacks and water will be available for members and staff taking part. We will be sitting on the Parliament Hill lawn, so please bring a blanket or lawn chair if you need one. Please note that expenses for this event are not eligible for reimbursement. For more information about the event on Parliament Hill, including a link to the live broadcast at 12:00 PM on September 30, please visit the NCTR’s website.

85176.title: NR Place de Ville Sub-Group 2026 AGM
85176.description: Hello everyone, We are inviting engineers, architects and land surveyors who are members of the NR Place de Ville Sub-Group to attend their Annual General Meeting (AGM) to be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026. This is the time and opportunity for all of us to get together and review what we have done so far and plan what we may like to accomplish next year. Also, we will receive information on current initiatives being taken up by NR group and PIPSC, along with an update on the status of bargaining, towards renewal of our collective agreement. This is your Sub-Group, so come and get involved/participate. NR group bargaining coordinator will be joining us to provide an update on the current status of bargaining and will also be available for a Q&A session, providing members with an opportunity to ask questions and discuss issues related to the bargaining process. This is your Sub-Group, so come and get involved/participate. At the AGM, we will also be electing new Executive Committee Members, whose term may be expiring, setting the course activities for next year and voting on the budget and expenses of our subgroup. Where: Montgomery Legion, 330 Kent St. Ottawa, On. K2P 2A6 When: Thursday, October 1, 2026-4pm to 7 pm ET Refreshments / Dinner: Will be served, please indicate if you may have any dietary restrictions/allergies RSVP: In order to make necessary arrangements for the refreshments please confirm your attendance immediately upon receiving this notice or latest by Frid

85213.description: NOTICE OF ELECTION And ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING DATE: Thursday, September 17th, 2026 TIME: 5:00 PM LOCATION: Restaurant L’in-time, 299 rue de l’Église, Verdun, QC, H4G 2M3 ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING The 2026 Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) will take place on September 17th at 5:00 PM. A meal will be served after the meeting. Please note that no member will be admitted to the dinner unless they have previously attended the AGM in person. The restaurant operates on a bring-your-own-wine basis, and an SAQ store is located nearby. Mocktails and soft drinks are also available from the menu, but these will be at each participant’s own expense. The dining room is wheelchair accessible; however, there are two small half-steps at the restaurant entrance. Assistance can be provided to anyone who may need help entering the restaurant. As places for dinner are limited, please RSVP as soon as possible or no later than September 10th, 2026, by email to your executive at cpmontreal@pipsc.ca. You will find the Agenda, the Notice of Election and the Call for Applications for the available positions on the Executive a little further down. The provisional Minutes of the 2025 AGM will be sent out to participating members before the AGM. To expedite the process at the AGM, we encourage you to review the documents before the meeting.
